tasks.short: Inspect project sites and record conditions that affect cost estimates.

steps.what: Review plans and previous records; prepare a site inspection checklist.
Arrange site access, attendance and visit timing with the site contact.
Visit the site; record access, drainage, topography and visible utility conditions.
Confirm uncertain utility availability and access restrictions with responsible contacts.
Combine observations, photographs and confirmations into a draft site report.

loop.input: Recorded observations, photo references, confirmations and unresolved questions.
loop.output: A source-linked draft site report with explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Validate required sections and source references. Require support for each factual statement; retain contradictions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt. On validation failure, populate a template with original notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text observations need concise synthesis. Templates handle the report structure but cannot reliably summarize varied notes.

steps.what: Approve the site report and identify conditions requiring estimating allowances or specialist investigation.

tasks.design: A checklist generator uses approved templates and project references in the {DOCS}; configured scheduling in the {WORKFLOW} prepares visit arrangements. A mobile form in the {WORKFLOW} captures observations and photo references, while a bounded drafting loop prepares the report in the {DOCS}. The cost estimator approves the report and decides which uncertainties need allowances or specialist investigation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical conditions require a visit. Notes, photographs and confirmations also arrive separately, making report preparation awkward.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing mobile forms and document templates handle capture and assembly. AI coding can reduce implementation effort, and a bounded model loop can summarize recorded notes.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden services, ground conditions and utility capacity require reliable external evidence or specialist surveys. Software cannot establish these from photographs.
tasks.human_edge: Notice site conditions that the checklist misses, challenge assurances and judge when a specialist investigation is worth its cost.

ambition.what: Reassess site-risk allowances at design revisions using unresolved site questions.

tasks.altitude: Visits still dominate the work. Less report assembly leaves time to investigate expensive uncertainties; spending and bid approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate uncertain site conditions into contingency scenarios.
reach.learn: Scenario costing, contingency methods and how uncertainty affects the project budget.

evidence.claim: Site inspection depends on physical observation; structured capture can reduce paperwork without replacing the visit.
Templates and source-linked drafting can support report preparation; estimator-specific savings are not established by this digest.

assumptions: This task concerns construction or facilities projects within a mid-size European company.
The time shares describe a typical visit including local travel within the inspection step.
The estimate assumes existing document access and mobile forms; it excludes specialist survey equipment.
The solution records site conditions rather than monitoring employee performance.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Employee consultation depends on national rules and the actual deployment.
unknowns: Whether photography and mobile devices are permitted at project sites.
Which site records and utility confirmations are available before visits.
Whether the existing {WORKFLOW} supports offline capture.
Who can approve site-risk allowances and commission specialist surveys.
Whether national rules or employee agreements require consultation; any required consultation may extend the access range.
research_questions: Which missing observations have caused costly estimate revisions?
Can checklist-based reports preserve the detail needed by downstream estimators?
How reliably does the drafting loop preserve uncertainty and conflicting observations?
new_work: Review drafted reports against original observations.
Maintain inspection templates and required evidence fields.
Resolve incomplete uploads and broken photo references.
Maintain access, retention settings and drafting validation rules.

tasks.short: Maintain a reliable directory of suppliers, contractors and subcontractors for estimating.

steps.what: Collect existing supplier records and recent supplier changes.
Request missing contact, capability and qualification information from suppliers.
Match supplier identities and reconcile duplicate or inconsistent directory entries.
Assess capability and qualification evidence; decide supplier eligibility for the directory.
Update supplier categories, contacts, evidence links and approved status in the directory.
Circulate directory copies to estimators and project teams.

tasks.design: Use the {PROCUREMENT} as the shared directory, with scheduled imports from the {ERP} and structured update requests through the {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic checks validate fields, match stable identifiers and queue ambiguous identities for review; a procurement specialist approves eligibility changes before publication. Teams use the live directory, removing circulated copies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier records serve different purposes across estimating and finance. Unclear field ownership and spreadsheet copies allow duplicates and stale qualifications to persist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing supplier records, forms and validation rules can handle most of the workflow. AI coding can make field mapping and exception screens cheaper to build; no model loop is necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Legal entity changes, disputed capabilities and inconsistent qualification evidence need investigation. A complete record does not establish supplier reliability.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish credible capabilities from unsupported claims and resolve supplier identities using commercial context.

ambition.what: A supplier-coverage gap review by trade and operating region for upcoming bids.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends less time copying contacts and chasing routine updates, and more time finding gaps in available suppliers. Procurement retains supplier eligibility and purchasing approval rights.

reach.task: Map qualified supplier coverage against the upcoming bid pipeline.
reach.learn: Category design, coverage measures and the distinction between missing evidence and missing supply.

evidence.claim: Supplier directories can use existing records applications, structured forms and deterministic validation.
Stable identifiers support automatic matching, while ambiguous identities and capability assessments need human review.

assumptions: The company maintains supplier master records in the {ERP} and a sourcing directory in the {PROCUREMENT}.
A spreadsheet currently reconciles records between systems and teams.
The directory supports estimating and does not authorize purchases or change payment details.
Routine information requests use approved templates and contact rules; people handle unusual replies.
Build ranges assume supported exports or interfaces and an existing supplier-record capability.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Consultation under national rules depends on whether employee data practices change.
unknowns: Which system owns each supplier field and who resolves conflicting updates.
Whether supplier identifiers remain consistent across the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}.
Whether the {PROCUREMENT} supports the required categories, access controls and approval states.
Which qualification checks are mandatory for each supplier category.
How many historical duplicates need manual cleanup.
Whether employee consultation is required under national rules; required consultation may extend the access range.
research_questions: Which directory fields materially improve supplier selection for estimates?
What proportion of duplicate candidates can be resolved using stable identifiers?
Can suppliers complete structured updates without creating extra support work?
new_work: Resolve identity conflicts and rejected updates.
Review qualification gaps and eligibility changes.
Maintain category definitions, validation rules and field ownership.
Monitor failed imports, unanswered requests and stale records.
Maintain contact-data access and retention settings.

role.altitude: Physical inspection and commercial judgement remain central. The estimator gains time for site uncertainty and supplier coverage analysis; bid, purchasing and spending authority do not automatically expand.
reach: Budget analysts: connect site uncertainty to contingency scenarios.
Business intelligence analysts: connect supplier coverage to upcoming bids.
skills_to_grow: Structured evidence capture and source checking.
Supplier data quality and entity matching.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an early bid-readiness review combining unresolved site risks, contingency scenarios and supplier coverage gaps.
